openQuestions.question: WP-12 asks whether the idle frame stop may freeze exhibit motion mid-cycle (the Verafin bars). Ruling needed.
openQuestions.default: Yes. 15 s after the last input the canvas renders no more frames, wherever an exhibit is in its cycle; exhibits must not rely on frames after runtime.motion turns false (no ease-out to rest). The kit clock advances only while motion is true, so the next input resumes from the same pose with no jump. Rendering extra frames to finish a cycle would reopen the battery cost the idle stop exists to remove.

openQuestions.question: A3 after integration: with WP-11's environment the remount needs 5.3 to 7.0 s to reach ready on SwiftShader in this shared 4-CPU container (first load takes about 10 s). A CPU profile of the recovery shows getProgramInfoLog (synchronous program linking) at 4.8 s of 7.2 s for 21 programs; without the precompile it is 18 programs and still about 6 s, so the cost is the mandated remount, not WP-16 code. quality.spec (c) will fail at the WP-11 merge on a loaded machine.
openQuestions.default: Keep the 5 s threshold and judge it on the CI runners (2 workers); if CI also exceeds it, rule a SwiftShader allowance for (c) (for example 10 s) while real-GPU recovery stays well under 5 s.

openQuestions.question: The 2026-10-15 ruling says MuseumCanvas mounts QualityController inside <MaterialsProvider>; neither the base nor wp/WP-11 does yet.
openQuestions.default: Move <QualityController /> inside <MaterialsProvider> in MuseumCanvas.tsx (one line). PrecompileMaterials works in both positions: outside the provider it compiles a private library from the same factory, which warms the same programs (three shares programs by parameters); inside it uses the canvas's own instances.

openQuestions.question: CameraRig (base and wp/WP-15) calls invalidate() on every frame while not settled. When the scroll rests between two stops (desktop proximity snapping may leave it there), the canvas renders forever and the 15 s idle stop cannot apply.
openQuestions.default: Invalidate only while |progress.current - progress.target| > 0.0005, a glide or fade runs, or the rig animates (gaze, framing, dolly, parallax); FrameDriver already covers camera movement and compiles.

openQuestions.question: On an exhibit page the context-loss fallback sets data-mode="classic" and the store's mode to 'classic' (the static story shows, #app and the canvas are hidden by CSS, rendering stops), but the canvas stays mounted because MuseumGate is R6's.
openQuestions.default: MuseumGate unmounts MuseumCanvas when useMuseum mode is 'classic'.

openQuestions.question: The remount after a restore resets the store's ready and settled to false, so the new canvas signals ready again (ARCHITECTURE §13.4 describes ready as set once).
openQuestions.default: Accept: ready means the current canvas is ready; the stage fades back in when the new canvas is complete.

openQuestions.question: Rule 4 gives coarse pointers with fewer than 4 reported cores the low tier. Whether current iOS Safari reports navigator.hardwareConcurrency of at least 4 is not verified here.
openQuestions.default: Check data-tier on a real iPhone at G5 (the WP-32 checklist); keep the rule unless it lands on low.

openQuestions.question: Deviation: the flip-flop limit is counted in dpr.ts over real DPR changes, and drei's PerformanceMonitor gets no flipflops prop. drei increments its flip counter on every incline even at the DPR cap, so flipflops={3} would lock a fast device at DPR 1 after about 10 s of smooth rendering, and the counter restarts with each monitor mount.
openQuestions.default: Accept: more than 3 real changes in a session lock the DPR at 1 (the onFallback behaviour of ARCHITECTURE §8.4).

notes: Design: FrameDriver publishes {demand, run, motionActive} (frameDemand.ts) and never blocks another component's invalidate() except during a pause, so WP-15's rig-driven frames (gaze, framing, dolly, parallax, fade) keep rendering and the idle stop never cuts them; no R4 interface is needed. A pause (hidden tab, lost context, or the phone sheet once ready: html[data-sheet='open'] and openId both set, per the M2a ruling) switches R3F to frameloop 'never'; the return sets 'demand' and renders one frame. Coarse-pointer idle motion is paced at 30 fps by a requestAnimationFrame gate (33.3 ms minus 4 ms slack), which lands on every 2nd, 3rd or 4th frame at 60, 90 or 120 Hz; a plain 33 ms setTimeout would align to vsync at about 20 fps. lastInputAt writes are spaced 100 ms apart; the kit's useIdle and FrameDriver both key on it. The DPR monitor samples only steady runs (a fresh PerformanceMonitor per run; 30 fps bounds for coarse idle motion) and QualityController re-applies its DPR when a <Canvas> re-render resets the prop. PrecompileMaterials waits until the scene shows fog or a light (they are part of every program key), holds compilePending, and gives kit-filled texture slots a 1 x 1 stand-in on a clone. ExhibitFrame was verified to await gl.compileAsync before reveal (no R3 bug). The exhibit clock pause on visibilitychange is the kit's (useExhibitRuntime hides motion) plus FrameDriver's pause; contextLoss.ts runs the 5 s restore deadline only while the tab is visible (iOS restores contexts on return). ContextLossHandler writes data-generation on its canvas for tests and debug. Integration: a local trial merge of wp/WP-16 with wp/WP-11, wp/WP-15 and wp/WP-14 had no conflicts; on it camera.spec and dialog.spec pass on desktop, dialog, camera and environment specs pass on pixel7 after commit a2d69be (which fixed a cold deep link never reaching ready behind the phone sheet), and quality.spec passes except (c), see openQuestions. Medium and high tier captures differ only through WP-11's tier-dependent environment; DPR stays 1 under ?test=1 for every tier. Runs used PORT=4178 and --workers=1; npm run verify and npm run build pass; @smoke: 80 passed.
